description: Senior AI Engineer with deep RAG/LLM experience. Tests: domain-specific probing (embedding model selection, chunking strategy, vector DB migration rationale, MCP vs REST tradeoff).

config.role_context: LLM-powered product features; RAG pipelines, agent orchestration, and model serving for enterprise legal-tech

persona.name: Samuel Okonkwo
persona.summary: Deep AI/ML engineer. Can explain every modeling decision, benchmark, and tradeoff in technical depth — embedding model selection criteria, chunking experiments, pgvector migration rationale, MCP architecture choices.

project_knowledge.cv_item: Embedding model evaluation (4 models benchmarked, chose Cohere v3)
can_explain: The 7K annotated query-document benchmark construction (domain experts, inter-annotator agreement)
Why MRR over recall@k for legal queries (position of the first relevant doc matters for lawyer workflow)
Why Cohere v3 beat OpenAI on multi-hop: Cohere's training data includes more legal/professional domain text
The cost dimension: Cohere v3 was also 40% cheaper at their query volume
Why 512 not 256 or 1024: benchmarked all three; 512 had best recall@10 vs latency tradeoff
The BERT boundary detector: trained on section-break annotations; prevents splitting a clause mid-sentence across chunks
How he validated: ran the same 200 queries with and without boundary detection; 18% recall@10 improvement attributable to fewer mid-clause chunks
Tradeoff: the BERT classifier adds ~15ms per chunk at ingest time — acceptable because ingestion is async but adds cost at high volume
The specific problem: document updates in Postgres took 15-30min to propagate to Pinecone; stale embeddings caused hallucinations in legal context (dangerous)
Why pgvector: same Postgres instance, zero sync latency, IVFFlat indexing sufficient at their 2M chunk scale
What he benchmarked: QPS at 2M/5M/10M chunks with pgvector vs Pinecone; pgvector matched Pinecone up to 5M, degraded after
What he'd do differently at 50M+ chunks: would keep pgvector for freshness-critical chunks and add a dedicated ANN index (Qdrant) for scale

project_knowledge.cv_item: JurisMCP — MCP server for NZ legislation
can_explain: Why MCP over REST: coding agents and VS Code extensions need structured tool interfaces; MCP handles auth natively, no API-key management per integration
Tradeoff: MCP is new and evolving; REST has broader ecosystem support. Bet that agent tool-use will standardise on MCP
How he handled legislation structure: each statute section becomes an MCP resource; query tool uses hybrid keyword+semantic search over section embeddings

persona.answering_style: Conversational but precise. When asked 'why' he names the benchmark, the metric, the alternatives he tried, and what he'd change. Distinguishes personal decisions from team decisions naturally.

stage2_criteria.name: Smooth interview arc
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: The interview follows arc: greeting → get-to-know → CV deep-dive → technical probing → wrap.

stage2_criteria.name: Probes RAG architecture decisions
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: At least 2 questions probe specific RAG/LLM architecture decisions: embedding model choice, chunking strategy, retrieval evaluation methodology, vector DB tradeoffs, or MCP architecture. PASS if 2+ questions ask 'why did you choose X over Y' or 'how did you evaluate X' about specific technologies from the CV.

stage2_criteria.name: Probes evaluation methodology
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: The candidate's CV describes multiple benchmarks and evaluations (4-model embedding comparison, chunking recall, pgvector latency benchmarks). PASS if the interviewer asks at least one question about how something was MEASURED or EVALUATED or what the METRIC was.

stage2_criteria.name: References CV technologies by name
stage2_criteria.conversation_goal_prompt: At least 3 questions name specific technologies from the CV (pgvector, Pinecone, Cohere, MCP, BERT, LangChain, etc.). PASS if 3+.

sim_user.end_instruction: Participate fully. When wrap-up comes, ask about the team's current AI infrastructure, then call [END_CALL].
